data.description:
## Context / Problem

`src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` re-exports 7 names it does not define, each marked
`# noqa: F401  (re-exported for back-compat)` — 3 from `._processors_identity`
(`_rederive_keyring_keys`, `process_key_event`, `process_signature`) and 4 from
`._processors_status` (`_fold_claimed_session`, `_fold_close_metadata`,
`_fold_plan_review_phase`, `process_status`). ADR 0111 forbids internal shims.

Censused on `origin/main` at `50d5a36539d` by parsing every `.py` under `src`, `tests`
and `scripts` with `ast`, resolving relative imports, and separately scanning for
attribute-style access:

- **4 names have zero importers** and can be deleted outright: `_fold_claimed_session`,
  `_fold_close_metadata`, `_fold_plan_review_phase`, `_rederive_keyring_keys`.
- `process_key_event` — 1 importer, production: `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py:19`.
- `process_signature` — 5 sites: `_replay.py:19` plus
  `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13`,
  `tests/unit/test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15`, and `tests/unit/test_signing.py`
  at both `:117` and `:133`.
- `process_status` — 6 sites: `_replay.py:19` plus
  `tests/unit/test_attestations_reducer.py:13`, `tests/unit/test_claimed_session.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_harness_provenance.py:20`,
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_happy.py:6`, and
  `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10`.
- No attribute-style access (`_processors.process_status(...)`) anywhere.

A line-oriented grep for `from rebar.reducer._processors import <name>` reports 0
importers for `process_key_event` and misses `test_attestations_reducer.py` entirely,
because `_replay.py` and that test import inside multi-line parenthesized statements
where the name is on its own line. The AST census above is the correct instrument; the
grep count is not.

## Change

Repoint the 3 names that have importers to the modules that define them:
`process_key_event` and `process_signature` to `rebar.reducer._processors_identity`,
`process_status` to `rebar.reducer._processors_status`.

Three importers pull a genuine `_processors` member on the same statement and must be
split rather than rewritten wholesale: `_replay.py` imports 18 names of which only those
3 move; `test_legacy_signature_mirror_drop.py:15` and
`test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:10` each also import `process_snapshot`, which is
defined in `_processors.py` at `:469` and stays.

Then delete all 7 re-exports from `_processors.py`. The whole
`from ._processors_status import (...)` statement goes, since all 4 of its names are
re-export-only. The `._processors_identity` statement keeps `_bootstrap_genesis_keyring`,
`_fold_author_attribution` and `attestation_kind`, which carry no `noqa` because
`_processors.py` uses them.

Extend the held-out oracle `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py`, which
already covers `_processors`/`_processors_status` and establishes the convention: assert
the re-exports are absent AND that the canonical modules still expose them, so the
assertion cannot pass vacuously.

## Testing

- A case in `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py` asserting
  `not hasattr(_processors, name)` for all 7 names, paired with positive assertions that
  `_processors_identity` and `_processors_status` still expose them.
- The repointed test modules must stay green unchanged in substance — only their import
  lines move.
- `make verify` covers the whole-tree effect, including the reducer replay suites that
  exercise `_replay.py`'s dispatch.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] **AC1** No `noqa: F401  (re-exported for back-compat)` comment remains in
      `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`:
      `grep -cF 're-exported for back-compat' src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py` prints 0.
- [ ] **AC2** Re-running the AST census reports 0 importers for all 7 names.
- [ ] **AC3** `python -c "from rebar.reducer import _processors as p; assert not any(hasattr(p, n) for n in ['_rederive_keyring_keys','process_key_event','process_signature','_fold_claimed_session','_fold_close_metadata','_fold_plan_review_phase','process_status'])"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] **AC4** `python -c "from rebar.reducer._processors_identity import process_key_event, process_signature; from rebar.reducer._processors_status import process_status; from rebar.reducer._processors import process_snapshot"`
      exits 0, proving the moved names stay reachable canonically and `process_snapshot`
      is unaffected.
- [ ] **AC5** `ruff check src tests` exits 0 with no output.
- [ ] **AC6** `pytest tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py -q` exits 0 and its
      case count increases by exactly the number of cases added.
- [ ] **AC7** `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD` touches only
      `src/rebar/reducer/_processors.py`, `src/rebar/reducer/_replay.py`, the 6 named
      test modules, `tests/unit/test_internal_shims_removed_3a46.py` and
      `docs/release-notes.md`, and no other path.
- [ ] **AC8** `make verify` exits 0.

## Ordering

Independent of the resolver-shim story — different modules, no shared source file.
Either may land first.

## Out of scope

- `tests/unit/test_plan_review_phase_reducer.py:63`, which captures logs on the logger
  named `"rebar.reducer._processors"`. That record originates in `process_snapshot`,
  defined in `_processors.py` itself and using that module's own logger, so repointing
  these imports does not affect it and the string must not be changed.
- The `_engine_support/resolver.py` shim, tracked separately.
- Any behavior change in the processors themselves.
data.title: Repoint reducer _processors re-exports and delete them
